modifications: Target is bit-identity with mlx2's composed eager ops (fast rms_norm on float32 rows, weight multiply, bf16 round; qmv_fast down/inject; qmv up; prebuilt unary Sigmoid; JIT-compiled nn.silu; bf16 col_reduce_small sum; mean scale), not with omlx's previous kernels.

Launch 1 (norm_down): one threadgroup of hidden/4 threads normalises all four streams with rms_single_row's lane mapping and reduction (the eager path normalises each stream in its own 640-thread threadgroup), so every threadgroup holds the whole normed row; each simdgroup then runs whole qmv_fast down rows (no K slices: omlx's per-stream K slices change the add order), lane 0 applies /hc and the compiled SiLU in bf16; one extra threadgroup runs the four inject rows and 2*sigmoid(raw/hc).

Launch 2 (up_mix): one simdgroup per hidden column runs the four qmv up rows with qmv's full-block-plus-tail order and simd_sum, then lane 0 applies sigmoid, the bf16 stream product, the bf16 stream sum in col_reduce_small order (p0+0, then p_j + total) and the mean's *0.25 (omlx: coalesced chunk staging and a shuffle-down FP32 mix).

Two sigmoid variants: the prebuilt unary kernel is compiled -fno-fast-math, so its metal::exp is the precise one; the JIT-compiled nn.silu resolves metal::exp like any metal_kernel. Each variant equals its eager counterpart over all 65,536 bf16 inputs and the other one differs at one input (GPU table in the check script).

Rows follow MLX's matvec choice for the folded M: one row transcribes qmv_fast/qmv (law 0); 2..8 rows on Apple GPU family 15+ transcribe qmv_wide (law 1: k_lanes 8, per-group 8-value dequantised sub-chunks, shuffle-down ladder 4/2/1), so a verify window equals its own composed call, not one-row decode, as in the composed path. Other row counts (qmv_nax from 12 rows on M5, qmm, unknown GPU family, MLX_QMV_LIMIT set) are declined and counted. omlx instead serves 1..6 rows bit-equal to its own one-row kernels.

The pending residual write (#4024 deferred write, omlx's _NDNW load) is not folded in: _apply_inject stays composed (PENDING_WRITE_SEAM documents the meeting point with the separate raw-gate+inject work).
Both launches run as one mx.compile function per launch geometry with the weights as inputs (2.3 us of host per call vs 5.7 us for two metal_kernel calls).

Admission is structural and refuses with a counted reason: rows != 1, non-bf16 input, training, non-eager norm (fused group norm on, fast RMS norm off/width), compiled glue on, layout (hc 4, hidden % 128 == 0 and <= 4096, width % 512 == 0, lowrank not a multiple of 512 and not 64/128, exact nn.QuantizedLinear 4-bit gs64 affine with bf16 scales/biases, not lane-owned), no Metal. The layout verdict and launch plan are cached per module keyed on the identity of every child, child class and child array.
First call per specialization is evaluated inside a try; a failure demotes the path for the process (counted).

2026-10-01 (lane W3, mixed-precision artifacts): every projection may be 4- or 8-bit affine group 64 independently (down DB, up UB, quantized inject IB template constants). 8-bit rows transcribe MLX's bits == 8 arithmetic: qmv_fast with 8 values per lane per 256-value block (down, inject), plain qmv with 4 values per lane per 128-value block and the guarded tail (up rows, lowrank 320 is not a whole 8-bit block), qmv_wide's 8-value sub-chunk dequantize s * q + b. Admission follows MLX's per-format choice (qmv_fast_k_alignment 512 / 256). The 4-bit arithmetic is unchanged.

2026-10-01: a dense bf16 block_inject_weight (nn.Linear, no bias; the uncensored artifact keeps it unquantized) runs in norm_down's inject threadgroup (INJ = 2): at one row MLX's GEMVKernel tiling for this shape (8 simdgroups over K, lane l of simdgroup g owns 4 columns per 1024-column block, rows accumulate inter * v in order, shuffle ladder 16..1, simdgroups 1..7 added onto simdgroup 0 in order), at 2..8 rows GemvWide (one inject row per simdgroup, 8 float4 dot per lane per 256-float4 step, halving shuffles). Admitted when the width is whole 1024-column blocks and >= 16 * hc. Row-exact windows run the one-row gemv per row. Mixed formats in one module (8-bit down/up with a dense or 4-bit inject, 4-bit down/up with an 8-bit inject) are admitted; any other format declines with a counted reason (bits / inject: ...).
2026-10-01: status gains calls_by_format (e.g. 'down b8 up b8 inject dense').
